What you get for free

  • In-depth lessons

    650 lessons across all 64 events, each built around the official HOSA test plan or rating sheet, with diagrams, interactive activities and checkpoint questions.

  • Full-length practice tests

    88 original Round One simulations with 4,400 questions, every one explained and referenced. They run slightly harder than the real test so competition day feels easier.

  • Rules in one place

    The current 2026–27 HOSA guidelines for each event, linked from the event page so you always study from the source of truth.

  • Graders for skills and speeches

    Upload, skills video and speech tools for performance events, so you can get feedback between chapter practices.

  • Mr. DNA, your study buddy

    An animated study companion that answers questions about your event while you work.

  • Progress tracking

    See which lessons and tests you have finished and where your score is weakest.

How to study for HOSA with Valus

  1. Choose your event. HOSA students compete in one event a year, so Valus is shaped around a single focus.
  2. Read the rules. Start with the current official guidelines for your event.
  3. Work through the lessons. Each unit follows the test plan, so your time goes where the points are.
  4. Take a practice test. Review every explanation, then retake the topics you missed.
  5. Practice with your chapter. Your advisor can assign work and follow your progress.
